issues.description: Sensitive payment card data (cardNumber, cvv) stored in plain object without encryption. PCI-DSS compliance requires card data must never be stored unencrypted in application code.
issues.suggestion: Never handle raw card data in your application. Use a PCI-compliant payment processor (Stripe, PayPal) that provides tokenization. Replace PaymentDetails interface with a payment token reference: { paymentToken: string; amount: number; }

issues.description: CVV (Card Verification Value) must NEVER be stored according to PCI-DSS standards, even temporarily. This is a critical compliance violation.
issues.suggestion: Remove CVV from the interface entirely. Payment processors handle CVV validation server-side and never return it to your application.

issues.description: Function accepts and processes raw payment card data, creating PCI-DSS compliance liability. Any system handling raw card data requires extensive security controls and annual audits.
issues.suggestion: Refactor to use payment processor tokens. Example: processPremiumPayment(userId: string, paymentToken: string, tier: ...) and call external payment API with the token.

issues.description: Card number validation is insufficient and insecure. Only checking length allows invalid card numbers. Missing Luhn algorithm validation.
issues.suggestion: Remove all card validation from your code. Let the payment processor handle validation. If you must validate, use a PCI-compliant library and implement Luhn algorithm.

issues.description: Date comparison bug: expiryDateObj uses month-1 but doesn't set day, defaulting to day 1. Card expires at start of expiry month instead of end, causing valid cards to be rejected.
issues.suggestion: Set expiry to last day of the month: const expiryDateObj = new Date(2000 + parseInt(year), parseInt(month), 0);

issues.description: Year 2000 issue: parseInt(year) + 2000 fails after year 99 (2099). Will incorrectly calculate dates as 2100+ when it should wrap.
issues.suggestion: Use proper century calculation: const currentCentury = Math.floor(new Date().getFullYear() / 100) * 100; const fullYear = currentCentury + parseInt(year);

issues.description: Logs full error object which may contain sensitive payment data (card numbers, CVV) in error.context or error.data. This violates PCI-DSS logging requirements.
issues.suggestion: Never log full error objects in payment code. Use sanitized logging: console.error('Payment failed: Transaction ID:', transactionId); Implement proper error tracking with PII redaction.

issues.description: Storing last 4 digits of card is acceptable under PCI-DSS, but the full card number is still in memory and potentially logged/cached. Memory dump or error could expose full cardNumber.
issues.suggestion: Accept only tokenized payment reference from client. If you must store last 4 digits, receive it pre-masked from payment processor: { last4: string; brand: string; }

issues.description: No authentication/authorization check before processing payment. Any userId can be passed without verification that the requesting user owns that userId.
issues.suggestion: Add authentication context: processPremiumPayment(authenticatedUserId: string, ...) and verify: if (authenticatedUserId !== userId) throw new UnauthorizedError('Cannot process payment for another user');

issues.description: No authentication check before granting feature access. Function trusts userId parameter without verifying the caller is authenticated as that user.
issues.suggestion: Add authentication: hasFeatureAccess(authenticatedUserId: string, feature: string) or use middleware to inject authenticated user context.

issues.description: No authentication/authorization before retrieving subscription data. Allows any user to query any other user's subscription details.
issues.suggestion: Add authentication context parameter and verification. Consider implementing role-based access: only the user themselves or admins should access subscription data.

issues.description: Database query uses parameterized queries ($1, $2, $3) which is good, but no transaction handling. Payment charge and subscription upgrade are separate operations that could leave inconsistent state if one fails.
issues.suggestion: Wrap payment processing in database transaction: const client = await db.getClient(); try { await client.query('BEGIN'); /* payment + upgrade */ await client.query('COMMIT'); } catch(e) { await client.query('ROLLBACK'); throw e; }

issues.description: No idempotency protection. Multiple calls with same payment info could charge customer multiple times if function is retried due to network failure.
issues.suggestion: Implement idempotency key: Accept idempotencyKey parameter, check if payment with that key already exists before processing.

issues.description: Payment amount validation allows exact match but doesn't handle floating-point precision errors. Could allow underpayment due to 0.01 rounding differences.
issues.suggestion: Use integer cents for money calculations: amount: number (in cents), or use a decimal library like decimal.js.

issues.description: Hardcoded tax rate (8%) and processing fee (2.9%). Tax rates vary by jurisdiction and change over time. Processing fees vary by payment method.
issues.suggestion: Move to configuration: const config = { taxRate: process.env.TAX_RATE || 0.08, processingFee: 0.029 }; Better: Calculate tax based on user's location.

issues.description: Floating-point arithmetic for money calculations can cause rounding errors (0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30000000000000004). Can lead to incorrect charges.
issues.suggestion: Use integer cents throughout: const basePrice = PRICING[tier] * 100; const tax = Math.round(basePrice * TAX_RATE); return (basePrice + tax + fee) / 100;

issues.description: Feature list is hardcoded in two places (premium and enterprise). Adding/modifying features requires code changes in multiple locations.
issues.suggestion: Move to configuration object: const TIER_FEATURES = { free: [], premium: ['unlimited_todos', ...], enterprise: [...] };

issues.description: Hardcoded subscription duration (1 year). No support for monthly subscriptions or custom durations. Business logic inflexibility.
issues.suggestion: Add duration parameter: upgradeUserSubscription(userId, tier, durationMonths = 12). Calculate: validUntil.setMonth(validUntil.getMonth() + durationMonths);

issues.description: Using JSON.stringify() to store arrays in database. Poor queryability - cannot efficiently query subscriptions by feature without full table scan and JSON parsing.
issues.suggestion: Use proper database schema: Create subscription_features junction table with (subscription_id, feature) rows for efficient queries.

issues.description: JSON.parse() called on every feature access check. For frequently accessed features, this causes unnecessary parsing overhead and CPU usage.
issues.suggestion: Cache parsed subscription data: Use Redis or in-memory cache with TTL. Or restructure database to avoid JSON storage.

issues.description: Database query on every hasFeatureAccess call. For pages checking multiple features, this causes N database queries. Performance bottleneck.
issues.suggestion: Batch feature checks: hasFeatureAccess(userId, features: string[]) returns Map<string, boolean>. Or cache subscription at request start.

issues.description: No rate limiting on payment processing. Vulnerable to abuse - attacker could spam payment attempts, causing charges, failed attempts, or DoS.
issues.suggestion: Implement rate limiting: Use middleware or library (express-rate-limit) to limit payment attempts per user/IP. Example: max 5 attempts per hour.

issues.description: chargeCard function simulates payment gateway but doesn't integrate with real payment processor. Production code should use Stripe, PayPal, or similar.
issues.suggestion: Integrate real payment processor: const stripe = require('stripe')(process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY); const charge = await stripe.charges.create({...});

issues.description: SELECT features, valid_until query fetches only needed columns (good), but could benefit from database index on user_id for faster lookups.
issues.suggestion: Add database index: CREATE INDEX idx_subscriptions_user_id ON subscriptions(user_id);

issues.description: SELECT * fetches all columns including potentially large JSON fields when only some fields may be needed by callers.
issues.suggestion: Use explicit column selection: SELECT user_id, tier, valid_until, features FROM subscriptions WHERE user_id = $1.

issues.description: Date comparison (validUntil < new Date()) doesn't account for timezone differences. Could cause off-by-hours errors for users in different timezones.
issues.suggestion: Store timestamps in UTC in database, compare using UTC: validUntil.getTime() < Date.now().

issues.description: JSON.parse() without try-catch. If database contains corrupted/invalid JSON, function throws unhandled exception, crashing request.
issues.suggestion: Add error handling: try { const features = JSON.parse(subscription.features); return features.includes(feature); } catch (e) { return false; }

issues.description: JSON.parse() without error handling. Database corruption or manual data edits could cause parsing to fail and crash the function.
issues.suggestion: Wrap in try-catch: try { return { ...row, features: JSON.parse(row.features) }; } catch (e) { return { ...row, features: [] }; }

issues.description: Function assumes db.query returns array, but no type checking. If db.query returns undefined or different structure, rows.length will throw.
issues.suggestion: Add type guard: const rows = await db.query(...); if (!rows || !Array.isArray(rows) || rows.length === 0) return false;

issues.description: Function has multiple responsibilities: validation, payment processing, and subscription upgrade. Violates Single Responsibility Principle.
issues.suggestion: Split into smaller functions: validateAndProcessPayment(), upgradeSubscription(). Use a service/orchestrator pattern to coordinate.

issues.description: Generic error messages don't provide actionable information for users. 'Invalid payment details' doesn't indicate which field is invalid.
issues.suggestion: Return specific validation errors: if (!validateCardNumber(cardNumber)) throw new ValidationError('Card number must be 16 digits', 'cardNumber');

issues.description: Boolean return type loses information. Caller can't distinguish between different failure reasons (validation, network, insufficient funds).
issues.suggestion: Return detailed result object: type PaymentResult = { success: boolean; transactionId?: string; error?: { code: string; message: string } };

issues.description: File comment mentions no tests exist. Critical business logic involving payments MUST have comprehensive test coverage (unit + integration tests).
issues.suggestion: Create test file: premium.test.ts with tests for: payment validation, price calculation, payment success/failure scenarios, subscription upgrades, feature access checks.

issues.description: Database import suggests tight coupling. Payment/subscription logic directly depends on specific database implementation, making testing difficult.
issues.suggestion: Use dependency injection: export class SubscriptionService { constructor(private db: DatabaseInterface) {} }. This allows mocking in tests.

issues.description: Subscription interface lacks id field. Database subscriptions typically need unique identifiers for updates, auditing, and referencing.
issues.suggestion: Add id field: interface Subscription { id: string; userId: string; ... }. Use UUIDs or auto-increment IDs from database.

issues.description: Duplicate database query pattern across functions. getUserSubscription and hasFeatureAccess both query subscriptions table with similar logic.
issues.suggestion: Create shared helper: private async getSubscriptionFromDb(userId: string): Promise<SubscriptionRow | null> and reuse.

issues.description: No logging/auditing of payment attempts. For compliance and debugging, all payment operations should be logged (without sensitive data).
issues.suggestion: Add audit logging: logger.info('Payment attempt', { userId, tier, amount, timestamp }); Use structured logging library like winston or pino.

issues.description: No webhook or event system for subscription changes. Other parts of application may need to react to subscription upgrades (send email, update UI cache, etc).
issues.suggestion: Emit events: eventBus.emit('subscription.upgraded', { userId, tier, validUntil }); Use event-driven architecture for decoupling.

codeQuality.summary: CRITICAL SECURITY ISSUES: This code has severe PCI-DSS compliance violations by handling raw payment card data (cardNumber, CVV) in application code. This creates massive legal and security liability. The code also lacks authentication/authorization checks, allowing any user to process payments or access any other user's data. Multiple high-severity issues include: no transaction handling (risk of charging without upgrading subscription), no idempotency (risk of double-charging), insufficient error handling, and vulnerable to various attacks. Performance issues include inefficient JSON storage in database and lack of caching for frequently-accessed data. Maintainability problems include tight coupling, hardcoded business logic, insufficient test coverage for critical payment logic, and floating-point arithmetic for money. IMMEDIATE ACTION REQUIRED: 1) Replace all card handling with payment processor tokenization (Stripe/PayPal), 2) Add authentication/authorization to all functions, 3) Implement database transactions for payment operations, 4) Add comprehensive test suite, 5) Refactor to use dependency injection for testability.

testCoverage.summary: CRITICAL: Zero test coverage for payment and subscription management system. This file contains 7 functions (5 exported, 2 internal) handling critical business logic including payment processing, card validation, pricing calculation, and feature access control. All 29 identified code paths are untested, with 18 being CRITICAL priority (financial transactions, security, access control) and 9 HIGH priority (validation edge cases, boundary conditions). Immediate risks include: (1) Payment processing bugs causing financial loss or fraudulent charges, (2) Invalid card validation allowing bad transactions, (3) Pricing calculation errors causing revenue loss or overcharging, (4) Access control failures granting unauthorized premium features, (5) Expired subscription handling allowing continued access. Recommended action: Implement comprehensive test suite with mocked database (db.query) covering all payment flows, validation edge cases, pricing calculations for both tiers, error handling paths, and feature access control scenarios before deploying to production.

suggestions.description: Introduce Repository Pattern and Payment Gateway abstraction to separate payment processing from database operations. This makes the code more testable and follows Dependency Inversion Principle.
suggestions.benefits: Separates concerns, enables dependency injection for testing, allows swapping payment gateways without changing business logic, makes mocking trivial in tests

suggestions.description: Introduce Strategy Pattern with individual validators and Result type for better error reporting. Current implementation only returns boolean without explaining what failed.
suggestions.benefits: Each validator is independently testable, provides specific error messages for better UX, follows Open/Closed Principle (easy to add new validators), separates validation concerns

suggestions.description: Extract pricing configuration into a PricingStrategy pattern. Magic numbers and business rules should be configurable and testable separately.
suggestions.benefits: Separates pricing configuration from calculation logic, enables different tax rates per tier if needed, easier to test calculation logic independently, rounds to proper currency precision

suggestions.description: Extract expiry date parsing logic into a separate function for reusability and testability.
suggestions.before:
const [month, year] = expiryDate.split('/');
const expiryDateObj = new Date(2000 + parseInt(year), parseInt(month) - 1);
suggestions.benefits: Reusable function that can be tested independently, clearer intent, includes radix parameter for parseInt (best practice)

suggestions.description: Use Result/Either pattern for better error handling instead of throwing exceptions and returning booleans. This makes error handling explicit and type-safe.
suggestions.benefits: Type-safe error handling, callers forced to handle errors explicitly, no throwing exceptions for expected business logic failures, provides structured error information for better UX

suggestions.description: Extract feature mapping into a configuration object and introduce Repository pattern. The hardcoded features array should be configurable.
suggestions.benefits: Centralizes feature configuration, introduces repository pattern for database operations, makes features easily maintainable, enables easier testing through dependency injection

suggestions.description: Use optional chaining, early returns, and extract subscription validation logic.
suggestions.benefits: Reuses repository pattern, clearer business logic, extracted subscription validation for reusability, eliminates JSON parsing duplication

suggestions.description: Eliminate code duplication by reusing the SubscriptionRepository introduced in earlier refactoring.
suggestions.benefits: Eliminates code duplication, single source of truth for database queries, easier to maintain and test

suggestions.description: Add branded types for sensitive data and use readonly for immutable properties. Create a TierType union for reusability.
suggestions.benefits: Type-safe handling of sensitive data, prevents accidental misuse of card numbers/CVVs, readonly ensures immutability, centralized tier type definition reduces duplication

suggestions.description: Introduce Service Layer pattern to coordinate between repositories and business logic. The current approach mixes concerns.
suggestions.before: // Functions directly call database and mix business logic
suggestions.benefits: Complete separation of concerns, all dependencies injectable for testing, single class coordinates complex workflows, easy to mock all dependencies in tests, follows SOLID principles

refactorings.summary: The premium.ts file contains critical payment and subscription logic with significant refactoring opportunities. Major issues include: (1) No separation between business logic, data access, and external service calls - introducing Repository and Service Layer patterns would dramatically improve testability; (2) Payment validation and processing lack proper abstractions - Strategy pattern for validators and Gateway pattern for payment processing would allow better testing and flexibility; (3) Error handling mixes exceptions and boolean returns - implementing a Result type provides type-safe error handling; (4) Hardcoded configuration values mixed with logic - extracting pricing and feature configurations improves maintainability; (5) Code duplication in database queries - Repository pattern eliminates this; (6) Missing type safety for sensitive data - branded types prevent misuse of card numbers/CVVs. Implementing these refactorings would transform untestable code into a well-structured, SOLID-compliant architecture where each component has a single responsibility and can be tested in isolation.

recommendations.description: Replace raw payment card handling with PCI-compliant payment processor tokenization (Stripe, PayPal, or similar). The current implementation stores and processes unencrypted card numbers and CVV, creating severe compliance violations and legal liability. This is a blocking issue that must be resolved before production deployment.

Add authentication and authorization checks to all functions. Currently, any user can process payments for other users, access any user's subscription data, or check feature access without verification. Implement user context validation in processPremiumPayment, hasFeatureAccess, and getUserSubscription functions.

Create comprehensive test suite for all payment and subscription logic. With 0% test coverage on critical financial code, there's extreme risk of bugs causing financial losses, fraudulent charges, or unauthorized access. Prioritize tests for payment processing, card validation, pricing calculations, and feature access control. Create src/premium.test.ts with mocked database dependencies.

Implement database transactions for payment operations. Currently, payment charging and subscription upgrade are separate operations without transaction boundaries, risking scenarios where customers are charged but don't receive their subscription (or vice versa). Wrap all payment processing in BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK blocks.

Add idempotency protection to prevent double-charging customers. Network failures or retries could cause the same payment to be processed multiple times. Implement idempotency keys that are checked before processing payments.

Refactor to use dependency injection and Service Layer pattern. Current tight coupling to database implementation makes testing impossible. Introduce SubscriptionService class with injected SubscriptionRepository, PaymentGateway, and PaymentRepository dependencies to enable proper unit testing and maintainability.

Implement rate limiting on payment processing endpoints to prevent abuse. Without rate limits, attackers could spam payment attempts causing DoS, excessive charges, or overwhelming the payment gateway. Limit to 5 payment attempts per hour per user.

Add proper error handling and validation for JSON parsing and database operations. Multiple locations parse JSON without try-catch blocks, risking unhandled exceptions if database contains corrupted data. Wrap all JSON.parse() calls in error handlers.

Replace JSON storage with proper relational schema for features and add database indexes. Current JSON.stringify/parse approach prevents efficient querying and causes performance overhead. Create subscription_features junction table and add indexes on user_id columns.

Extract hardcoded business logic (tax rates, processing fees, feature lists, pricing) into configuration objects or environment variables. Current hardcoded values make it difficult to adjust pricing, add features, or support different tax jurisdictions without code changes.

Replace floating-point arithmetic with integer cents calculations for all monetary operations. Floating-point rounding errors can cause incorrect charges. Use integer cents throughout calculations and only convert to dollars for display.

Replace mixed error handling (thrown exceptions + boolean returns) with Result type pattern for type-safe error handling. Current approach makes it difficult for callers to handle different failure modes. Implement Result<T, E> type with discriminated unions for error cases.
